paragraphs: AgentExpt tackles a consequential part of AI research: choosing datasets and comparison methods that fit a research question. These choices shape what an experiment can establish and how its results compare with other work. Resource descriptions alone often miss suitability, because the same dataset or method can serve different purposes in different studies.

The framework builds on a knowledge base connecting 108,825 accepted papers with the baselines and datasets they used. Its retriever combines each resource’s own description with descriptions found in papers citing it. This gives retrieval both the resource’s intended purpose and evidence about how researchers actually use it. A subsequent ranking model learns from reasoning chains connecting baselines and datasets and supplies explanations for its recommendations.

The reported experiments show average improvements of 5.85% in Recall@20 and 7.90% in HitRate@10 over the strongest baseline. Component-removal experiments also support the contribution of the proposed parts. Together, these findings support using scholarly usage context and explicit reasoning to improve experimental-resource recommendations.
icml-2026-agentexpt-automating-ai-experi.tldr: AgentExpt recommends experimental baselines and datasets by combining their descriptions, scholarly usage contexts, and reasoning about how they fit together.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning can improve a model’s answers while narrowing the range of solutions it explores. This paper examines that collapse in methods such as GRPO, attributing it to reverse KL minimization: an objective that tends to concentrate learning around a rewarding solution already discovered. Finding one successful route can therefore suppress exploration of other useful strategies.

DMPO changes the distribution that training tries to match. Within a sampled group of reasoning trajectories, it assigns target probabilities proportional to rewards and trains the policy toward that distribution. This approximates forward KL minimization, which favors covering multiple rewarding possibilities. Constructing the target within a sampled group avoids needing samples from an inaccessible global target distribution.

On NP-Bench, DMPO achieves Quality Ratios of 43.9% for text and 43.1% for vision, compared with GRPO’s 40.1% and 38.4%. The paper also reports gains on mathematical reasoning and out-of-domain tasks. These experiments support the claim that preserving exploration can improve solution quality across the evaluated reasoning settings.
icml-2026-beyond-mode-collapse-distribut.tldr: DMPO trains reasoning models to cover multiple rewarding solution paths, improving exploration and reported reasoning performance.

paragraphs: Learning causal relationships from time series becomes harder when observations arrive at uneven intervals or are missing. Filling gaps requires assumptions about how variables relate, while discovering those relationships depends on the filled values. Errors can reinforce each other: an inaccurate completion can suggest a misleading causal graph, which can then encourage further inaccurate completions.

ReTimeCausal addresses this dependence through an expectation-maximization framework that alternates between completing the data and learning causal structure. It combines kernel-based sparse regression with structural constraints, updating each part in light of the other. The aim is to encourage agreement between the completed observations and the relationships inferred from them throughout optimization.

The paper provides theoretical consistency guarantees for structure recovery, extending classical results to irregular sampling and substantial missingness. It also reports better performance than existing methods on synthetic and real-world datasets under challenging sampling conditions. The contribution connects the two estimation problems explicitly, with theoretical and empirical support for the resulting recovery process.
icml-2026-causal-discovery-for-irregular.tldr: ReTimeCausal alternates missing-data completion and causal graph learning to encourage consistency when time series are irregularly sampled.

paragraphs: Before estimating a treatment’s causal effect, one must establish whether the available observations determine that effect at all. Hidden confounders complicate this question because they can influence both treatment and outcome. This paper asks what can be identified using only the joint distribution of those two observed variables, without additional variables that satisfy special structural requirements.

The analysis focuses on linear structural causal models. Within that setting, the authors organize the possibilities according to whether the external noise terms are Gaussian. Their conditions are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive, providing a complete classification within the studied framework. The classification distinguishes situations with an identifiable causal effect from those in which multiple effects remain compatible with the observations.

For the unidentifiable cases, the paper also determines how many feasible solutions remain. That describes the extent of ambiguity, rather than stopping at a yes-or-no verdict. Empirical results validate the theoretical findings. The central message is conditional: noise distributions can determine identifiability in these linear models even without auxiliary observations.
icml-2026-causal-effect-identifiability-.tldr: For linear causal models with hidden confounders, the paper characterizes when treatment–outcome observations alone identify a causal effect.

paragraphs: Collaborative perception lets multiple agents combine what they observe, but their sensors and models may produce incompatible features. Mapping every feature type into a shared representation seems helpful. However, independently trained converters can retain modality-specific patterns, so features that supposedly share a format still disagree in meaning. These mismatches can accumulate during fusion.

CauseCollab approaches this problem by separating semantic information from statistical factors associated with the sensing modality. Its causal metric learning formulation aims to disentangle those factors within the shared protocol space. A context-guided unified converter then handles heterogeneous modalities while promoting agreement in their semantic representations. Adding a new modality requires training an adapter with relatively few parameters.

Experiments on OPV2V and DAIR-V2X report state-of-the-art performance, with larger gains when modalities differ substantially. This pattern supports the motivation for explicitly addressing modality-related inconsistency. The practical contribution is a shared conversion framework that targets the meaning of exchanged features while keeping the adaptation required for new modalities small.
icml-2026-causecollab-causal-unified-and.tldr: CauseCollab improves collaborative perception by separating shared semantic content from modality-specific effects in exchanged features.

paragraphs: Many time-series foundation models learn to forecast each variable separately. This supports strong forecasting for individual series, but leaves relationships between variables underused. ChaTSFM adds a lightweight channel adapter so an existing, frozen forecasting model can draw on those relationships when making multivariate forecasts in a zero-shot setting.

The adapter is pretrained on a budgeted dataset designed to contain varied dependencies between channels. It uses descriptors derived from the data to condition its measure of channel similarity on the dataset. This addresses the problem that a similarity measure suitable for one domain can become distorted in another. Sparse information from other channels then enters through a gated refinement mechanism that preserves the model’s within-channel temporal dynamics.

Across nine benchmarks, the paper reports consistent zero-shot improvements for four strong foundation models while retaining scalable deployment. These findings support adapting how a pretrained model combines variables without updating its underlying parameters. The approach makes cross-variable information available through a small additional component, preserving the usefulness of the frozen forecasting backbone.
icml-2026-channel-adapter-for-time-serie.tldr: ChaTSFM adds a lightweight adapter that helps frozen time-series models use relationships between variables for zero-shot forecasting.

paragraphs: High-resolution images present a search problem for multimodal models: important evidence may occupy a small region. Expert-assisted search can locate promising areas efficiently but miss relevant content when its proposals fail. Scanning the whole image offers coverage, yet can waste computation and divide meaningful objects across artificial boundaries.

CVSearch coordinates these strategies without additional training. It first assesses whether the global view supplies enough information. If more detail is needed, it invokes expert-assisted search; semantic-aware scanning follows only if that search fails. Its adaptive patching divides images into regions that respect semantic content, reducing object fragmentation. A bottom-up search process then uses a visual-complexity prior to guide iterative exploration of local details.

The reported high-resolution benchmark results show state-of-the-art accuracy together with substantially improved search efficiency. The approach matters because it makes the search procedure conditional on what has already been learned. Expensive exploration is reserved for unresolved cases, while the fallback scanning mechanism addresses blind spots left by expert proposals.
icml-2026-cvsearch-empowering-multimodal.tldr: CVSearch adaptively combines expert-guided search and semantic-aware scanning to improve high-resolution image understanding without additional training.

paragraphs: Thermal image restoration must contend with image degradations that can change and accumulate over time. Methods designed around a fixed set of degradations struggle when unfamiliar ones appear. ECMRNet treats restoration as continual learning, organizing adaptation around three operations: expanding the model, compressing redundant capacity, and reusing knowledge learned previously.

The network separates intermediate representations into isolated groups. When learning a new degradation, it freezes historical groups and adds new ones with a matching structure. To control growth, Structural Entropy Pruning removes redundant channel groups according to their information contribution. A separate knowledge-mining module retrieves and recombines useful components from historical representations to handle images affected by compound degradations.

Experiments report superior overall restoration across diverse individual and compound degradations, with fewer parameters and lower computation. The three components address connected demands: accommodating new corruption types, limiting accumulated model size, and transferring earlier knowledge to combinations of corruptions. The results support this coordinated approach to ongoing adaptation in thermal restoration.
icml-2026-expandable-compressible-mineab.tldr: ECMRNet continually adapts thermal image restoration by adding isolated capacity, pruning redundancy, and recombining previously learned degradation knowledge.

paragraphs: Protein design often starts by generating a structure and then finding an amino-acid sequence for it. A structure can be designed around a functional goal, yet the subsequent sequence model may not account for that goal. Multiple sequences can correspond to a structure, making structural compatibility alone insufficient to resolve the functional design choice.

FIDIA incorporates functional constraints into reinforcement-learning rewards and aligns training with Best-of-N inference, where several candidates are generated and the best is selected. Its gradient estimator directly targets the expected maximum reward among candidates. This makes the learning objective reflect the selection procedure used at inference, while steering sequence generation toward regions with high functional fitness.

On a general motif-scaffolding benchmark, FIDIA consistently improves success rate and precision over standard and reinforcement-learning-optimized baselines. Additional experiments address vaccine design and enzyme designs intended to enhance affinity. These findings support combining functional objectives with selection-aware training for the studied protein-design tasks, including the reported therapeutic and biocatalytic cases.
icml-2026-fidia-function-informed-sequen.tldr: FIDIA optimizes protein sequence design for functional goals and the Best-of-N selection procedure used at inference.

paragraphs: Video understanding models often have enough computation to inspect only a small selection of frames. Uniform sampling can miss relevant moments, while giving every question the same frame budget ignores differences in difficulty and information density. FrameOracle learns both which frames matter for a query and how many frames the model needs.

The module follows a training curriculum that begins with weaker signals, including similarity between text and visual content. It then uses stronger supervision from FrameOracle-41K, a video question-answering dataset with validated annotations identifying minimal sufficient frames for each question. These annotations teach frame selection and budget prediction together, linking the amount of visual evidence to the question being answered.

Across five vision-language models and six benchmarks, FrameOracle reduces 16-frame inputs to 10.4 frames on average without losing accuracy. Starting from 64 candidates, it selects 13.9 frames on average and improves accuracy by 1.5%. The results show that query-dependent selection can reduce input size while preserving or improving answer quality.
icml-2026-frameoracle-learning-what-to-s.tldr: FrameOracle learns which video frames a question requires and adjusts the frame budget to reduce computation while preserving accuracy.

paragraphs: Evolutionary multi-view classification searches among candidate solutions using fitness evaluations. Incorrect training labels can undermine this process twice: they provide harmful supervision and distort the fitness landscape guiding the search. The paper calls the resulting distortion fitness evaluation bias and argues that it can misdirect evolution toward local optima.

Motivated by discrepancies between human and model decision boundaries, GFD-EMVC uses a detect-then-calibrate procedure. First, it identifies outliers in gradient space and treats them as potentially noisy samples. It then uses feature-space prototypes built from noise-free samples to correct the suspected labels. The two stages draw on different signals: training behavior identifies suspicious examples, and learned representations guide their correction.

Experiments show that this purification strategy can reduce label noise and alleviate fitness evaluation bias. The paper also reports improved performance across multiple multi-view learning paradigms under noisy labels. Its contribution is to connect data cleaning with the evolutionary search process, showing that better supervision can also make the search’s quality judgments more useful.
icml-2026-gfd-emvc-evolutionary-multi-vi.tldr: GFD-EMVC detects suspicious labels through gradient outliers and corrects them using feature prototypes to improve learning and evolutionary search.

paragraphs: Matching a person across visible-light and infrared videos requires handling both sensor differences and changes over time. Pose variation and occlusion introduce structure within each video tracklet. The paper argues that conventional Euclidean representations distort the hierarchy in these temporal variations, weakening the representation used for matching identities across modalities.

Hyperbolic Hierarchical Alignment places temporal modeling and modality alignment in the Poincaré ball, a hyperbolic representation space. Its spatio-temporal aggregator organizes changing visual cues hierarchically through geometry interaction and dual-geometry fusion. A second component aligns the modalities in two ways: it couples their centroids to promote geometric consistency and anchors both to shared identity prototypes to support discrimination between people.

Experiments on HITSZ-VCM and BUPTCampus report state-of-the-art performance. The approach joins two closely related requirements: preserving the organization of changes within a person’s video and keeping visible and infrared representations comparable. The stated findings support using a common geometric framework for both requirements in the evaluated cross-modality identification setting.
icml-2026-hyperbolic-hierarchical-alignm.tldr: HHA uses hyperbolic representations to organize temporal variation and align person identities across visible and infrared videos.

paragraphs: Combining language-model agents can fragment the knowledge and rules governing their actions. Judgment Operators address this at decision time through four possible interventions: allow an action, edit it, escalate it, or deny it. A portable artifact supports these interventions without changing agent internals, including minimal repairs when an action can be corrected.

The paper establishes composition-invariant enforcement with constant violation probability, sublinear mistake accumulation through JO-A, and semantic preservation for code transformations. Programmatically verifiable constraints underpin these formal results. A necessity lower bound motivates the enforcement design by showing that decentralized schemes cannot achieve constant violation probability within the theoretical setting.

Empirically, the framework records no observed violations, compared with 48–68% for baselines; this observation is distinct from a universal zero-violation guarantee. The paper also reports 13.5–20.5% zero-shot cross-model transfer where few-shot prompting fails, and partial-mediation results better than the theoretical worst case. Together, the findings support a portable interface for governing and repairing actions across composed agent systems.
icml-2026-judgment-operators-a-compositi.tldr: Judgment Operators govern multi-agent actions through portable allow, edit, escalate, and deny decisions, with formal results for verifiable constraints.

paragraphs: Some classification problems provide several views of each example and allow multiple labels, while leaving parts of both the inputs and annotations missing. LGRL addresses this setting by using available labels to shape representation learning throughout the model. The motivation is that partial annotations carry semantic structure beyond their role as targets for prediction.

The framework learns category prototypes and uses them to construct a mixture prior that guides representation extraction. It also builds category-specific conditional posteriors, with prototypes serving as Bayesian experts when information from multiple views is combined. These components let category information influence both what each representation captures and how evidence from different views is fused.

A label-driven information-bottleneck objective balances retaining enough information for reconstruction with consistency across views. This supports reasoning conditioned on particular categories despite incomplete observations. Experiments demonstrate effectiveness on benchmarks and applications in sports analytics and medical imaging. The contribution is a coordinated use of label semantics across representation extraction, information fusion, and the learning objective.
icml-2026-label-guided-representation-le.tldr: LGRL uses category prototypes and label semantics to guide learning when examples have missing views and incomplete labels.

paragraphs: Principal component analysis can be strongly affected when a small fraction of observations comes from a distribution with a shifted mean. The resulting leading components may reflect that contamination instead of the original covariance structure. This paper studies the problem in a high-dimensional mixture setting where existing robust PCA approaches cannot handle the stated contamination structure.

The proposed solution deliberately adds a knockoff mean-shift perturbation. Random matrix theory provides the rationale: the authors prove that mean-shift spikes can be separated spectrally from the stable eigenvalues of the original covariance. They also show that the original eigenspace remains asymptotically invariant to contamination, independently of the mixture weight within the studied setting.

These properties yield a two-stage algorithm that identifies and removes the mean-shift component using standard PCA operations. Adding a controlled perturbation becomes a way to expose the unwanted structure. The theoretical claim concerns asymptotic spectral stability, and the algorithm uses that stability to distinguish contamination-related components from the original covariance eigenspace.
icml-2026-mean-shift-pca-by-knockoff-mea.tldr: The paper uses deliberately added mean-shift perturbations and spectral stability to identify and remove contamination from PCA.

paragraphs: Collaborative perception depends on agents sharing useful intermediate features, yet different sensing modalities can produce features that do not combine directly. Existing approaches often require a new adapter or additional training when a modality appears. Repeating this process is costly, especially when manufacturers cannot freely exchange their models or data.

UniTrans learns a universal mechanism for constructing feature translators. It pretrains a bank of expert parameters and predicts how to combine them for a particular source-to-target modality mapping. An intrinsic encoder extracts codes from single-frame intermediate features that describe the modality while remaining invariant to the scene. Those codes guide translator construction in a zero-shot manner.

Experiments on OPV2V-H and DAIR-V2X report consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods in simulated and real-world settings. The central idea is to reuse learned translation expertise through input-dependent combinations. This supports the paper’s goal of handling heterogeneous feature exchanges with one model, reducing the need to train a separate translator whenever the modality pairing changes.
icml-2026-one-model-to-translate-them-al.tldr: UniTrans constructs feature translators on demand by combining pretrained experts according to the source and target modalities.

paragraphs: Changing the timbre of one part in a musical mixture requires locating that part while preserving the surrounding accompaniment. The paper finds that ordinary cross-attention in diffusion-based music editing captures a stem’s semantic identity but lacks enough spectral precision to isolate it in dense mixtures. As a result, edits can leak into other components.

Polyphonia combines semantic attention with a probabilistic acoustic prior. The prior establishes coarse boundaries for the intended target, and attention calibration uses that acoustic guidance to support more localized synthesis. The framework performs zero-shot editing, addressing the need to change a specific musical component without allowing diffuse attention to spread the change across the mixture.

The authors introduce PolyEvalPrompts, a standardized collection of 1,170 timbre-transfer tasks in polyphonic music. On the reported evaluation, Polyphonia improves target alignment by 15.5% over baselines while retaining competitive music fidelity and non-target integrity. The evidence supports more accurate targeting, with preservation assessed empirically rather than established as a perfect guarantee.
icml-2026-polyphonia-zero-shot-timbre-tr.tldr: Polyphonia uses acoustic guidance to focus zero-shot timbre edits on a chosen musical stem while preserving competitive accompaniment integrity.

paragraphs: A short text query may describe only a small portion of an untrimmed video. This creates uncertainty both about which video is relevant and about which moments support the match. Vague queries can fit several videos, while sparse temporal supervision leaves the model with limited evidence for identifying the relevant clips.

Holmes models these uncertainties at two levels. Across videos, it treats similarity scores as evidence and represents that evidence with a Dirichlet distribution. Fine-grained identification of query characteristics then guides adaptive calibration during learning. Within a video, it uses flexible optimal transport to form soft alignments between the query and clips, with an adaptive dustbin helping suppress spurious local responses.

The combination gathers evidence at multiple granularities while reducing the influence of misleading local matches. Experiments report improvements over state-of-the-art retrieval methods. The approach matters because it explicitly represents uncertainty in matching brief language to rich video content, connecting decisions across candidate videos with denser evidence inside each video.
icml-2026-revisiting-uncertainty-on-evid.tldr: Holmes models uncertainty across videos and within their clips to improve retrieval when a text query describes only partial video content.

paragraphs: Panoptic video scene graph generation identifies relationships between entities represented at pixel level. Two properties make this difficult: meaningful interactions may appear only briefly, and some relationship categories have few training examples. A model must therefore locate sparse evidence in time while learning categories that are poorly represented in the data.

SegPVSG addresses the two problems with complementary components. TempFocusNet first localizes salient temporal segments and then recognizes relationships within them, concentrating processing on the relevant interactions. Relation-centric Generative Video Augmentation creates realistic segments depicting rare relations and inserts them coherently into existing videos. This adds training examples while retaining consistency with the surrounding video context.

The method improves over prior approaches by 3.53 in mR@20 and 5.9 in mR@50. These reported gains support pairing temporal localization with targeted augmentation for underrepresented relationships. The framework’s contribution is to organize learning around the short segments where relations occur and strengthen the available evidence for categories that otherwise receive little training coverage.
icml-2026-segpvsg-panoptic-video-scene-g.tldr: SegPVSG improves video relationship recognition by focusing on salient moments and generating contextual training segments for rare relations.

paragraphs: This paper studies whether a single universal adversarial perturbation can redirect multiple independent decisions by a multimodal language model. The targeted behavior depends on the meaning of the input: different semantic cases are steered toward different attacker-selected outputs. The question is especially relevant to stateless systems, where the decisions do not rely on retained conversational state.

The proposed Semantic-Aware Universal Perturbation acts as a semantic router. The authors analyze geometric properties of the model’s latent space theoretically and empirically, then use those findings to develop the Semantic-Oriented optimization strategy. They also annotate a dataset with fine-grained semantic labels to evaluate this form of input-dependent redirection.

Experiments across three representative multimodal models establish the attack’s feasibility. The reported Qwen result reaches a 66% attack success rate over five targets using a single frame. This demonstrates the studied possibility of one perturbation supporting multiple semantic destinations; the result is a measured success rate in the evaluated setting, rather than evidence of reliable control over every decision.
icml-2026-semantic-router-on-the-feasibi.tldr: The paper demonstrates that one adversarial perturbation can steer a multimodal model toward different attacker-selected outputs depending on input semantics.

paragraphs: Extending a language model’s context window does not necessarily make it equally reliable at every position. The paper finds that standard long-context fine-tuning can leave accuracy strongly dependent on where relevant evidence appears, even when task format and difficulty are controlled. This makes placement itself a source of brittleness in long-context understanding.

RoPE-Perturbed Self-Distillation creates alternative views of a training sequence by changing its rotary position indices. These changes effectively move portions of the context to different positions. A self-distillation objective encourages consistent predictions across the resulting views, pushing the model to rely more on semantic evidence and less on fragile associations with absolute placement.

Experiments adapting Llama-3-8B and Qwen-3-4B show consistent benchmark gains. Reported improvements include up to 12.04 percentage points on RULER-64K for Llama and 2.71 percentage points on RULER-256K for Qwen after supervised fine-tuning. Improved extrapolation beyond the training window further supports positional consistency as a useful training objective for long-context adaptation.
icml-2026-shuffle-the-context-rope-pertu.tldr: RoPE-Perturbed Self-Distillation improves long-context robustness by training models to agree across different positional views of the same sequence.

paragraphs: Language models ordinarily execute their layers once in a fixed sequence. This paper investigates alternative execution programs built from the same pretrained layers, allowing modules to be skipped or repeated. It reports that, for most inputs studied, substantially shorter programs can match or exceed standard accuracy, and some originally incorrect answers can be corrected with fewer executed layers.

These observations motivate PoLar, a lightweight prediction network that generates an execution program for each input. The pretrained layers supply the computational modules, while the predictor learns how to arrange their use through skipping and looping. The existence of alternative programs is demonstrated without retraining the layers; efficiently choosing programs in practice involves learning the predictor.

On mathematical reasoning benchmarks, PoLar consistently improves accuracy over standard inference and earlier dynamic-depth methods, often using fewer layers. The gains also persist in out-of-distribution evaluation. The findings suggest that useful reasoning computations can be accessed by varying layer execution, with fixed-depth inference using only part of the model’s available computational flexibility.
icml-2026-skip-a-layer-or-loop-it-learni.tldr: PoLar learns input-dependent programs that skip or repeat pretrained model layers, improving mathematical reasoning accuracy often with fewer layer executions.

paragraphs: Vision-language models spend substantial inference computation processing visual tokens. Removing many tokens can discard useful information, break spatial organization, and reduce diversity. SpecFlow approaches compression as condensation: it selects a smaller representation while explicitly enforcing spatial coverage and conserving statistical information from the tokens that are removed.

The framework treats tokens as nodes in a nearest-neighbor graph. Spectral heat flow produces a stable importance field that preserves structural coherence. Adaptive spatial partitioning assigns token budgets across image regions to guarantee coverage. Information from discarded tokens is then aggregated into retained representatives called coreset sinks. The procedure requires no training or fine-tuning and is compatible with FlashAttention.

Experiments report improvements over state-of-the-art methods across tasks, model architectures, and pruning ratios. For LLaVA-1.5, SpecFlow retains 95.6% of original performance while pruning 88.9% of visual tokens. This result supports the value of preserving information through aggregation when reducing visual sequence length, rather than treating token removal solely as a selection problem.
icml-2026-spectral-heat-flow-for-conserv.tldr: SpecFlow compresses visual tokens through graph-based importance, spatial coverage, and information aggregation, retaining strong performance under heavy pruning.

paragraphs: Neural molecular-dynamics potentials can learn many-body interactions, yet their GPU execution can lag behind classical force fields. FlashSchNet identifies movement between high-bandwidth memory and on-chip memory as a central bottleneck. Its design reorganizes SchNet-style computations to reduce repeated work, intermediate storage, and contention during accumulation.

Four techniques implement this approach. Fused radial-basis computation calculates each pairwise distance once and reuses it. Fused message passing avoids storing intermediate edge tensors in high-bandwidth memory. Segment-based aggregation reduces atomic writes by a factor equal to the feature dimension and supports contention-free accumulation. Channel-wise 16-bit weight quantization further increases throughput with negligible reported accuracy loss.

On one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000, FlashSchNet reaches 1,000 nanoseconds per day in aggregate across 64 replicas of a 269-bead coarse-grained protein. This is 6.5 times faster than CGSchNet with 80% less peak memory. In the reported setting, it surpasses widely used classical force fields such as MARTINI while retaining SchNet-level accuracy and transferability.
icml-2026-textttflashschnet-fast-and-acc.tldr: FlashSchNet accelerates neural molecular dynamics by reducing GPU memory traffic and fusing computations while retaining SchNet-level accuracy.

paragraphs: Implicit in-context learning seeks to reproduce the benefits of examples in a prompt through changes inside a model’s representations, aiming for few-shot performance at zero-shot cost. Existing methods often inject shift vectors derived from labeled demonstrations or task-specific alignment. This paper argues that such approaches underuse the structural mechanisms behind in-context learning and generalize poorly.

In-Context Routing instead operates on attention logits, the scores that govern how attention is distributed. It extracts reusable structural directions that arise during in-context learning. A learned router, conditioned on the current input, uses those directions to modulate attention scores. The resulting framework is designed to be trained once and reused across tasks.

Evaluation spans 12 real-world datasets from diverse domains and multiple language models. ICR consistently outperforms existing implicit methods that need task-specific retrieval or training, and shows robust generalization on out-of-domain tasks where those methods struggle. These findings support attention-level structure as a reusable basis for internalizing in-context learning behavior.
icml-2026-train-once-reuse-everywhere-ge.tldr: In-Context Routing learns reusable, input-dependent attention adjustments that improve implicit in-context learning across tasks and domains.
